fields.value: The paper frames focus of attention as a synchrony-based mechanism for selecting an interaction partner and locating the synchronized region of motion; it presents immediate synchronous imitation as a communication tool.

fields.value: An autonomous neural network architecture uses camera-derived optical flow and an oscillator model. A phase-locking value tracks synchrony; learned image-to-oscillator prediction supports partner selection, while spatial movement prediction and a winner-takes-all selection determine the attention direction.

fields.value: The paper presents a Nao robot that uses optical flow and synchrony to select a moving interaction partner and direct its focus of attention toward that agent. In tests with a human and a one-degree-of-freedom automaton, the robot synchronized with the agent whose movement frequency was close to its learned frequency, and its attention direction followed that agent.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper describes synchrony-based attention and partner selection, reports how the robot’s attention follows the synchronized agent, and details the sensing and neural-network implementation. It identifies the Nao platform but does not describe how embodiment shaped the study.
